plan.summary: This 4-week block fits the first building phase of a 12-week off-camp boxing plan. With only one 45-minute S&C session each week and more sparring in the overall load, the goal is to build usable lower-body and trunk strength, simple explosive intent, and basic work capacity without adding unnecessary fatigue. Week 1 is used to establish a simple bodyweight performance baseline, and the main progression starts in Week 2.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general strength, trunk control, and simple explosive qualities with low-equipment, low-fatigue work that supports boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress unilateral strength and power output while keeping the single weekly session crisp and recoverable around sparring.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength, sharpen speed and intent, and use lower-fatigue explosive work to express the force built earlier.

exercises.name: 1a. Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can with a soft landing. Reset between reps and stop if height drops off.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the countermovement jump feels awkward. Start from a still quarter squat and jump fast.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low stable box if landing mechanics are cleaner than floor jumps.

exercises.name: 1b. Shadowboxing Speed Burst
exercises.notes: Throw fast clean combinations with full intent and relaxed shoulders. Keep output sharp, not sloppy.

exercises.name: 2. Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: This week establishes your baseline. After warm-up reps, perform one hard top set per side with the hardest bodyweight version you can do cleanly for 6-10 reps, stopping one rep before form breaks. Log reps and setup used.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the hardest clean set per side and the setup you used so future weeks can progress from it.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if balance or rear-foot-elevated setup is not stable yet.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a knee-height or lower step if split squat positions bother the knees.

exercises.name: 3a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use the hardest clean variation you can control and stop with 1-2 reps in reserve. Keep the body straight and lower under control.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use hands on a bench, table, or sturdy surface if floor push-ups are too hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Knee Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if needed to keep full range and clean trunk position.

exercises.name: 3b. Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Drive through the heel and pause briefly at the top. Keep the hips level.

exercises.name: 4. Side Plank
exercises.notes: Stack the body in a straight line and keep the ribs down. Stop before the position twists.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if side plank position is too shaky.

exercises.name: 5. Forward-Backward Line Hops
exercises.notes: Stay light and springy off the floor. Small quick contacts, quiet feet, and stop if rhythm falls apart.

exercises.name: 1a. Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump hard every rep and stick the landing. Rest enough to keep height high.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the countermovement jump still feels more natural from a paused start.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low stable box if that lets you express power with cleaner landings.

exercises.name: 1b. Shadowboxing Speed Burst
exercises.notes: Fast hands, fast feet, relaxed face. Keep technique crisp while moving at top speed.

exercises.name: 2. Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use the same setup as Week 1 if it was challenging but clean. Slow on the way down, drive up fast.

performanceTarget.prompt: Beat last week by cleaner reps, a harder setup, or better control.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rear-foot-elevated work is still too unstable.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a stable step if split squat mechanics are not consistent yet.

exercises.name: 3a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Stop with 1-2 reps in reserve. If all sets are easy, progress to a harder variation next week.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor reps are still short of the target range.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a 3-second lowering phase if regular push-ups are already very easy.

exercises.name: 3b. Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Pause for one second at the top and keep the pelvis steady.

exercises.name: 4. V-Up or Tucked Leg Raise
exercises.notes: Move with control and keep the lower back from slamming into the floor.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the harder trunk flexion options are not controlled yet.

exercises.name: 5. Forward-Backward Line Hops
exercises.notes: Fast feet and short ground contact. Stay springy without turning it into a conditioning grind.

exercises.name: 1a. Skater Jump to Stick
exercises.notes: Jump sideways with intent, then own the landing for a full second. Keep the knee tracking clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Lateral Bound to Stick
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have enough space and can land cleanly.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if single-leg landing quality is not ready for lateral work.

exercises.name: 1b. Shadowboxing Speed Burst
exercises.notes: Fast sharp combinations with active feet. Keep the last few seconds as crisp as the first few.

exercises.name: 2. Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a controlled lowering phase and stand up hard. Stay tall and keep pressure through the front foot.

performanceTarget.prompt: Match the target reps with cleaner depth and balance before making the variation harder.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rear-foot-elevated reps still drift or lose balance.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a stable box or step if that lets you train the legs harder with better form.

exercises.name: 3a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use the hardest variation that keeps full range and leaves 1-2 reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Decline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are clearly too easy.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you still need a more manageable variation for clean reps.

exercises.name: 3b. Reverse Snow Angel
exercises.notes: Lift the hands off the floor if possible and squeeze the upper back. Move slowly and keep the neck relaxed.

exercises.name: 4. Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Press the lower back into the floor and keep the ribs tucked. Shorten the lever if needed.

substitutionOptions.name: Tucked Hollow Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the full hollow position is not yet controlled.

exercises.name: 5. Split Stance Iso Hold
exercises.notes: Hold a strong split-squat position with even pressure through the front foot. Stay still and brace.

exercises.name: 1a. Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Keep every jump snappy and leave plenty in the tank. This is a deload week.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simpler reset-based jump.

exercises.name: 1b. Shadowboxing Speed Burst
exercises.notes: Short, fast, sharp bursts. Finish fresher than you started.

exercises.name: 2. Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use an easier setup than Week 3 and move cleanly. Keep tension but cut fatigue.

performanceTarget.prompt: Use this week to recover and own the movement. Save harder progressions for the next block.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want the easier deload option.

exercises.name: 3a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Choose a variation that feels smooth and leaves 2 reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need the easiest clean deload option.

exercises.name: 3b. Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Controlled reps with a short pause at the top.

exercises.name: 4. Side Plank
exercises.notes: Hold a clean stacked position and stop early if shaking gets excessive.

exercises.name: 5. Forward-Backward Line Hops
exercises.notes: Stay light and relaxed. This should feel quick, not tiring.
